title: Near-duplicate cosine threshold for the split freeze (handshake H1)
criterion_preregistered: tau is fixed BEFORE the search runs and is never adjusted after seeing the candidate list. Primary value tau = 0.98 on cosine similarity between L2-normalised full-image RAD-DINO CLS embeddings (C07, variant full_clahe0), comparison '>=' so a pair landing exactly on tau is a candidate. Because Person 1 reviews every candidate by hand (P1-07), a lower tau costs review effort but not correctness, while too high a tau silently misses real duplicates and nobody ever learns. The threshold sweep at 0.95/0.96/0.97/0.98/0.99 is therefore run first, and this rule decides the final value: if the band [0.95, 0.98) adds 150 or fewer cross-split pairs, tau is lowered to 0.95 and all of them are reviewed; otherwise tau stays at 0.98 and the number of pairs left unreviewed in that band is recorded here and reported in the limitations section.

value.scope: cross-split pairs only; within-split duplicates are counted and reported but do not block the split freeze
value.split_precedence: train < development < calibration < internal_test < challenge_test; the later split loses the image

sweep_result.run_on: 2026-10-06, provisional official train/val/test splits, 12,278 images, variant full_clahe0
sweep_result.rule_outcome: 13 <= 150, so the rule lowers tau from 0.98 to 0.95 and all 158 candidates are reviewed by hand (P1-07).

why_full_image_not_crop: A lung crop discards the borders, collimation edges and burned-in markers that make two scans of the same patient distinguishable from one file stored twice, which is exactly the signal this search needs.
data_used: tbx11k images only, no labels, purpose=dedup (the single exception to the sealed-split guard, contract rule 4.1)
note: Rule applied 2026-10-06 on real embeddings. tau = 0.95 was DECIDED BY THE PRE-REGISTERED RULE, not chosen from the output: the sweep was run first and the rule in criterion_preregistered selected the value. tau is now fixed and must not move again. Re-running on Person 1's real C01 will change the candidate COUNT, because train/development/calibration/internal_test is a finer partition than train/val, but it must not change tau. What the pass found is more serious than a threshold question: 133 of 145 cross-split pairs have cosine 1.0000 and the twelve strongest are byte-identical files, so TBX11K stores the same image under two names in two different splits. See docs/p2_duplicate_finding.md. Still to lock: Person 1's review (P1-07) and the guide acknowledgement.
